correctness.rationale: The rank-two determinant lemma and zero-regularization expansion yield the exact inverse-trace identity, with every denominator positive. The explicit Boolean-cube heat kernel strictly increases both Laplacian resolvent differences with Hamming distance. The discrete maximum principle gives 2C<NB^2 for all distinct anchors, proving strict monotonicity of the trace for any positive a,b. Exact beta integrals and a low-gain expansion yield the stated sharp last-bit penalty. The supplementary package checker performs 481 exact rational tests, including direct inverses; finite tests are corroboration, not the proof. The scope excludes d=1 and zero feedback.

originality.rationale: The exact 2014 preprint derives equal-feedback joint centrality and explicitly gives equal-gain extremal pair intuition for equivalent-centrality graphs, which is acknowledged as prior coverage. The current claim strictly compares every Hamming-distance class for arbitrary unequal feedback strengths, with an exact weak-gain one-bit penalty; this is not supplied by inspected primary statements or relevant indexed records. Full statement-to-implication comparison, rather than word matching, supports a best-knowledge originality assessment with remaining specialized-literature risk.
residual_risks: A little-indexed theorem on two-pinning of distance-regular graphs may imply the result without mentioning Boolean cubes or leader selection.

value.rationale: This is a complete, gain-ratio-independent all-distance ranking for placing two independently weighted leaders on a canonical high-dimensional network. Earlier equal-gain maximum-separation observations do not provide the ordering of every nonoptimal class for unequal strengths. The exact last-bit regret translates the structural theorem into a design sensitivity statement whose limit remains finite as both total stationary variances diverge. This meets a meaningful network optimization question, beyond a routine numerical table.
